content.comment_body: I'm not sure why, but on one [product_name] device the date was incorrect yesterday. Everything else worked normally, except the year was wrong. After transferring the current time from my PC, the year became correct. Does anyone know what causes this?
Is it a [article_no] 230V model? There are known firmware issues related to the date on this version. What is the firmware version of your [product_name]? Is it [version_no]?
Yes, that's right. It's a [article_no] model with firmware [version_no]. Is there a known problem with this combination?

From what I know, the [article_no] 230V model with that firmware version has issues with the year part of the date. If you want official information, you can submit a support request and get a direct response from [company_name].

Thank you for sharing this. If the problem only affects the date, it's not critical for me. On a different [product_name] with 24V I have a newer firmware. Is it possible to update the firmware myself?

Unfortunately, [company_name] does not offer firmware updates for these devices, including the latest [article_no]. The newest [article_no] has the product version ES5 and firmware [version_no], in which the issue should be fixed.
That's unfortunate. Thanks for the clarification.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have discovered a date (year) display issue on the [product_name] device, specifically with the [article_no] 230V version running firmware [version_no]. The incorrect year can be temporarily corrected by syncing with a PC, but the problem originates from a firmware bug that cannot be resolved by users as firmware updates are not available. The bug is minor but persistent until newer hardware or firmware is installed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the date and time to work reliably without errors and would like the ability to update firmware themselves in order to fix known bugs.
